Deep-tech startup Discovered Materials has raised USD9 million (INR 85 crore) in a seed funding round led by Lightspeed India Partners, with participation from Y Combinator, Peak XV Partners and global angel investors including Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram and Thariq Shihipar.

According to the company, its AI systems have developed new thermal materials in three months, with performance comparable to products that took years to develop. The funding comes as Indian deep-tech startups continue to raise capital across AI, mobility, healthcare and energy. Indian deep-tech startups had raised USD1.62 billion across 140 equity rounds by July 2026, according to the report.

Founded by Advaith Sridhar and Akash Ramdas, Discovered Materials is working on materials for thermal dissipation in AI chips, which can generate more than 140W/cm². The company is developing thermally conductive dielectric materials for 3D chip packaging. The company will use the fresh capital to expand its team and laboratory and scale its AI research agents.
